en.name: Dried tofu skin (yuba)
en.summary: Dried yuba keeps 4–12 months in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark cupboard, and 12 months in the freezer at −18 °C (0 °F). That pantry range is the general figure for dried foods rather than one published for yuba; a commercial packet of 腐竹 is usually labelled 6–12 months and its own date should win.
en.pantry: 4–12 months in an airtight container somewhere cool, dry and dark — and the warmer the room, the shorter the end of that range you should use. The brittle sticks and sheets are dry enough that nothing grows on them, so the real risks are moisture and rancidity: yuba is the skin lifted off simmering soy milk, so it is rich in soy oil, and that oil oxidises with warmth, light and air. Any softness, bending instead of snapping, a musty smell or visible mould means it has picked up moisture, and it goes out. Note that fresh, undried yuba is a completely different food — refrigerated, and good for only a few days.
en.fridge: No refrigerated timeline is published for dried yuba, and the fridge is usually the wrong place for it. A dry food taken in and out of a cold, humid cabinet collects condensation, and moisture is the one thing that turns brittle sheets into a mouldy packet. A cool dark cupboard in an airtight tin does the job better. If your kitchen is very hot all summer, freeze it rather than refrigerating it.
en.freezer: 12 months at −18 °C (0 °F) in a sealed bag, which is worth doing in a warm kitchen because it protects the oil-rich sheets from going rancid. Press the air out, and keep the pieces whole so they do not shatter into unusable fragments. Kept continuously frozen it stays safe well beyond that window. Always let the sealed bag come up to room temperature before opening it, so condensation forms on the bag and not on the yuba.
en.thawing: Let the sealed bag reach room temperature before opening. There is no need to thaw the yuba itself — it goes straight into the soaking water, which is how it is used in any case.
spoilage: Sheets that bend instead of snapping, meaning they have taken up moisture.
A musty or damp smell in the packet.
Any visible mould, in which case the whole packet goes out.
A sharp, crayon-like smell — rancid soy oil, which cannot be soaked out.
tips: Keep it in an airtight tin, not the opened plastic packet.
Soak in cool or warm water, not boiling, or the sheets disintegrate.
Snap-test a stick: brittle is good, bendy means damp.
Fresh yuba is a refrigerated product with a life of days — do not apply these figures to it.

faq.q: How long does dried bean curd stick keep?
faq.a: 4–12 months in an airtight container in a cool dry cupboard, or 12 months frozen at −18 °C (0 °F). Go by the packet date when there is one.

faq.q: Does dried yuba need to be refrigerated?
faq.a: No. The fridge adds condensation, and moisture is what ruins it. A cool dark cupboard in an airtight tin is better; in a very hot kitchen, freeze it.

faq.q: How can you tell if dried yuba has gone off?
faq.a: It should snap. If it bends, smells musty or shows any mould, it has taken up moisture and should be thrown out.

zh.name: 腐竹
zh.summary: 乾腐竹裝密封罐、放陰涼乾燥避光處可放 4～12 個月，−18 °C 冷凍是 12 個月。常溫那個區間是乾貨的一般數字，不是為腐竹公布的；市售包裝通常標示 6～12 個月，而包裝上的日期應該優先。
zh.pantry: 裝密封罐放陰涼、乾燥、避光處 4～12 個月——房間越熱，就越要往短的那端抓。脆脆的支條和薄片本身乾到長不出東西，所以真正的風險是受潮和油耗：腐竹是從煮著的豆漿表面挑起來的那層皮，富含大豆油脂，而那些油會因為溫度、光線和空氣而氧化。只要變軟、折得彎而不是應聲而斷、有霉味或看得到霉，就表示它吸了水氣，該丟。另外要注意：新鮮未乾燥的豆皮是完全不同的食物——要冷藏，而且只放得了幾天。
zh.fridge: 乾腐竹沒有公布的冷藏期限，而冰箱通常是錯的地方。乾貨在又冷又潮的櫃子裡進進出出會結露，而水氣正是把脆片變成一包霉的元凶。陰涼避光的櫃子加一個密封罐，效果好得多。如果你的廚房整個夏天都很熱，請冷凍而不是冷藏。
zh.freezer: 密封裝袋放 −18 °C 下 12 個月；在炎熱的廚房裡這很值得，因為它能保護富含油脂的豆皮不油耗。請壓出空氣，並盡量保持整片完整，免得碎成沒法用的細屑。只要全程沒退冰，超過這段時間仍然安全。開袋前一定要讓整袋密封著回到室溫，讓水氣凝在袋子上而不是腐竹上。
zh.thawing: 讓密封袋回到室溫再打開。腐竹本身不需要解凍——它反正是要泡水的，直接下水就好。
spoilage: 折得彎而不是應聲而斷，表示它吸了水氣。
整包聞起來有霉味或潮味。
看得到任何霉，整包丟掉。
聞起來刺鼻、有蠟筆味——那是大豆油油耗了，泡水也泡不掉。
tips: 用密封罐，不要就著拆開的塑膠袋放。
用冷水或溫水泡，不要用滾水，否則會爛掉。
折一根測試：脆就是好的，會彎就是受潮了。
新鮮豆皮是冷藏食品、只放得了幾天，不要把這裡的數字套上去。

faq.a: 密封放陰涼乾燥處 4～12 個月，或 −18 °C 冷凍 12 個月。包裝上有日期就以日期為準。
不用。冰箱會帶來結露，而水氣正是毀掉它的東西。陰涼避光的櫃子加密封罐更好；廚房非常熱的話請冷凍。
它應該一折就斷。如果會彎、有霉味，或看得到霉，就是受潮了，該丟掉。
